counterfactual_missing_items: R1 and R4 omit the positive anti-HCV and raised liver enzyme finding
R4 omits the oral lichenoid plaques and lip erosions
R4 omits the bandlike lymphohistiocytic infiltrate histopathology
decisive_items: Revealed raised liver enzyme levels and positive anti–hepatitis C virus antibody status
lichenoid plaques on the right angle of mouth, bilateral buccal mucosa
Dense bandlike lymphohistiocytic infiltrate in the papillary dermis
response.rationale: R2 uniquely combines the oral lichenoid mucosal findings, LP-compatible nail histopathology, and the anti-HCV/raised liver enzyme association, making it the most complete and specific diagnosis. R1 captures lichen planus but misses the HCV association, while R4 is limited to nail findings and omits the mucosal and histopathologic evidence that secure the diagnosis.

rejected.why: Correct for lichen planus but lacks the hepatitis C association explicitly supported by the laboratory findings.
Too narrow: only addresses nail involvement and omits the oral mucosal lesions, histopathologic bandlike infiltrate, and HCV serology.
